holidays.name: Bloomsday
holidays.description: Book lovers around the world dress in Edwardian outfits, eat gorgonzola sandwiches, drink burgundy, and read aloud from James Joyce's Ulysses. In Dublin, fans retrace the route of the book's hero, Leopold Bloom, through the city's streets and pubs.
holidays.origin: Ulysses takes place entirely on June 16, 1904, the day Joyce first walked out with his future wife, Nora Barnacle. In 1954, on the 50th anniversary, writers including Flann O'Brien and Patrick Kavanagh made a pilgrimage around Dublin. That outing started the tradition.
holidays.funFact: Joyce's 700-plus-page novel covers a single day, and Bloom's lunch of a gorgonzola sandwich and a glass of burgundy has become the festival's signature meal.

holidays.name: National Fudge Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in squares of rich, creamy, chocolatey fudge, whether it's classic chocolate, peanut butter, maple walnut, or something more daring. Eat it plain or stir it into ice cream, and feel free to share it, though you don't have to.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. Fudge itself is an American candy that is said to have started in the 1880s, when a candy batch meant for caramels went wrong and turned into something better.
holidays.funFact: Fudge became a college favorite in 1888, when Vassar student Emelyn Hartridge made a batch for a school event, and soon women's colleges were swapping fudge recipes.

holidays.name: World Sea Turtle Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the ancient, shell-wearing wanderers of the ocean. Conservation groups use it to spotlight nesting beaches, plastic-free seas, and the many ways people can help sea turtles survive.
holidays.origin: The day is observed on the birthday of Dr. Archie Carr, born June 16, 1909. He was a pioneering sea turtle biologist and conservationist. The Sea Turtle Conservancy, which he helped inspire, promotes the observance.
holidays.funFact: Sea turtles have been swimming the oceans for more than 100 million years, and females often return to nest on the same stretch of beach where they hatched.
